distractorExplanations.c: Faith does not outrank statute. The firm follows the practice when it is legal, and it does not carry out a step the law forbids.
distractorExplanations.d: A cousin who lacks authority does not approve or veto the rite. The firm follows the authorizing agent's lawful request, not a bystander's theology.

prompt: An ex-partner comes in alone, says the relatives will not print his name, and describes years of a bond the printed notice will leave out. He is shaking as he talks. Which loss is he living?

options.text: Sorrow that began while everyone still hoped for a recovery and the person was alive
Disenfranchised grief, a loss other people treat as if it does not count
Ordinary mourning that always looks identical in public mourners and in private ones
A completed mourning that ends once the chapel portion of the day is over

explanation: He is shut out of the notice, and the relatives are treating years together as if they do not belong on the record. That is disenfranchised grief: a loss other people treat as if it does not count, such as an ex-partner or a hidden bond.

distractorExplanations.a: Sorrow that starts before an expected death is a different pattern. His pain is that other people refuse to count a bond, not that he began mourning early.
distractorExplanations.c: Ordinary mourning does not have one public look, and that claim does not name this scene. The injury is that others treat his loss as if it does not count.
distractorExplanations.d: A chapel service does not finish this grief. The point is social non-recognition of the loss, not a clock that ends when the service ends.

prompt: A week after the committal the firm intends to telephone a spouse who asked for a human check-in, yet a coworker wants that call to open a pitch for a future contract. What is aftercare actually for?

options.text: Opening collections, with a warm tone as the lead-in before the unpaid balance is mentioned
Treating lingering sorrow yourself, as though the call made you the clinician at the table
Continuing the merchandise talk until the household agrees to buy an upgrade on the contract
Contact after the funeral that offers support, not a second sales call disguised as care

explanation: The spouse asked for a check-in a week after the committal, and a coworker wants that call to sell a future contract. Aftercare is contact after the funeral. It is support, not a second sales call disguised as care.

distractorExplanations.a: A collections call uses a caring tone to chase a balance. Aftercare is support after the funeral, not an accounts conversation dressed as concern.
distractorExplanations.b: Treating the sorrow as the clinician steps outside the director's role. Aftercare stays supportive contact, and clinical care belongs with a qualified clinician.
distractorExplanations.c: Continuing the merchandise talk turns the check-in into another sale. Aftercare is not a second sales call disguised as care.

prompt: Parents of a young adult who died by suicide ask what will be said if guests demand details, and an uncle wants the death notice to assign fault to somebody. How should that conversation be handled?

options.text: Supply the method and the scene so guests stop asking and the written record is complete
Let the uncle name who failed, because a cause will settle the guests who keep asking
Speak without blame or graphic detail, and let the family lead what they want said
Forbid any mention of the suicide, even if the parents want one plain, non-graphic sentence

explanation: The parents are deciding what guests will hear, and an uncle wants the notice to assign fault. A suicide death is discussed without blame and without graphic detail. The family leads what they want said.

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in the method and the scene adds graphic detail the parents did not ask to share. The family leads the wording, and the account stays non-graphic.
distractorExplanations.b: Letting the uncle assign fault is blame. The talk stays free of blame, and the parents, not a relative hunting a cause, lead what is said.
distractorExplanations.d: A total ban takes the wording away from the parents. If they want a plain, non-graphic statement, they lead that choice. Forced silence is not the rule.

prompt: A spouse is unsure whether seeing her wife will help her grasp what happened, and a relative insists the firm must embalm and require that viewing or nothing will feel real. What is a sound use of a viewing?

options.text: A viewing can help some families accept that the death is real; it is an option, not a requirement, and not a reason to require embalming
Require embalming and a viewing in every death so each household reaches the same sense that the death happened
Refuse every viewing, because seeing the person always harms mourning and only slows the paperwork that follows
Promise that one viewing will finish grief for every relative before the day of the funeral is over

explanation: The spouse is unsure, and a relative wants embalming and a viewing made mandatory so the death will feel real. A viewing helps some families accept that the death is real. It is an option, not a requirement, and not a reason to require embalming.

distractorExplanations.b: Making embalming and a viewing mandatory turns an option into a rule. Seeing the person helps some families accept reality; it is not required, and it is not a reason to require embalming.
distractorExplanations.c: Refusing every viewing denies a step that helps some families accept that the death is real. The choice stays with the family, and the director does not ban it.
distractorExplanations.d: No viewing finishes grief for every relative on a timetable. It can help some people accept that the death is real, and it remains a choice rather than a promise.

prompt: An apprentice who has covered nighttime removals for three straight weeks says each call feels heavier and he dreads the telephone, yet the supervisor tells him only to toughen up. What actually lowers that strain?

options.text: Praise the toughness line, because personal stamina is what removes this strain from funeral work
Meet repeated trauma and long on-call hours with workload changes and support, not a demand to toughen up
Assign him every hard removal from now on so more exposure will numb the dread faster
Have the supervisor name a condition beside the prep table and send him back onto the same nights

explanation: Three weeks of night removals have made each call feel heavier, and the supervisor's answer is to toughen up. Staff burnout rises with repeated trauma and long on-call hours. The useful response is workload and support, not a harder shell.

distractorExplanations.a: Praising the toughness line is the toughen-up miss. Repeated trauma and long on-call hours need a workload change and support, not a speech about stamina.
distractorExplanations.c: More hard removals increase the exposure that is already driving the strain. Numbing him with extra trauma is the opposite of workload relief.
distractorExplanations.d: Naming a condition beside the prep table is a label the supervisor should not assign. The lever is the rota and support, not a judgment in the prep room.

prompt: After the rite a newly bereaved widower presses an expensive watch into the arranger's hand, asks for dinner this weekend, and hints the estate can add private cash. Which limit has to hold?

options.text: Accept the watch as thanks, because refusing a gift from a grieving household is an insult
Keep a professional boundary; money, a gift, or a personal relationship with this newly bereaved family is the miss
Accept the dinner if the romance stays off the letterhead and never enters the chapel
Take the extra cash as a private tip that never appears on the statement of goods and services

explanation: The widower is newly bereaved and is offering a watch, a weekend dinner, and private cash. The director keeps a professional boundary. Money, gifts, or a personal relationship with a newly bereaved family is the miss.

distractorExplanations.a: Accepting the watch takes a gift from a newly bereaved person and crosses the professional boundary. A clear refusal is the limit, not fear of giving insult.
distractorExplanations.c: A weekend romance with a newly bereaved widower is a personal relationship the role does not allow, even if it stays off the firm's paper.
distractorExplanations.d: Private cash from the estate is the money boundary. A tip that never hits the statement is still the miss, and it hides the payment.

prompt: Two brothers shout about earth burial versus cremation and each one demands to be declared the winner, as their sister stands there holding the signed authority papers. What should the arranger do amid the fight?

options.text: Side with the louder brother so the room can clear before the next household arrives
Side with whichever brother offers to pay the whole invoice before the other can speak
Hold every decision until the brothers like each other again, however many days that takes
Stay calm, write down what was said, follow the authorizing agent, and do not pick the winner

explanation: The brothers want a winner declared while their sister holds the authorizing papers. When relatives fight, the director stays calm, writes down what was said, and follows the authorizing agent. The director does not pick the winner.

distractorExplanations.a: Volume is not authority. Choosing the louder brother picks a winner, which the director does not do. The authorizing agent is the person to follow.
distractorExplanations.b: Paying the invoice does not make a brother the authorizing agent. Following the payer picks a winner by money instead of following the papers.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting until they are friendly again stalls the decision for a peace that may not come. The director documents the fight and follows the authorizing agent.

prompt: The arranger leaves in tears, cancels the next two meetings, and says the caller's panic has become a personal emergency of the arranger's own. A peer asks what real empathy requires here. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: Empathy means taking on the panic until your own day is as wrecked as the caller's day
Empathy is understanding the feeling, not absorbing the family's crisis as your own emergency
Empathy means offering a fix so fast that the feeling never has to be named out loud
Empathy means staying polite and distant so no feeling is reflected back to the caller

explanation: The arranger has canceled other meetings because the caller's panic now feels like a personal emergency. Empathy is understanding the feeling. It is not absorbing the family's crisis as if it were your own emergency.

distractorExplanations.a: Taking on the panic until your day collapses is absorption, not empathy. Empathy understands the feeling and still leaves the crisis with the person living it.
distractorExplanations.c: A fast fix that skips the feeling is problem-solving ahead of understanding. Empathy grasps the feeling; it does not erase it before it is named.
distractorExplanations.d: Polite distance that reflects nothing is detachment. Empathy does understand the feeling; it simply does not swallow the crisis as your own emergency.

prompt: A daughter says she cannot stop replaying the final hour and asks whether she should speak with someone trained for that kind of distress. The arranger wants to help without taking over a clinician's job. What does a fitting referral include?

options.text: Tell her she needs therapy as a shove, then end the meeting before she can ask where to go
Name the condition you suspect and outline a treatment plan you will supervise yourself
Stay vague, suggest she look around town sometime, and never say what kind of help exists
Be specific and kind, stay inside the role, and name the kind of help plus how to reach it

explanation: She is replaying the final hour and asking about someone trained for that distress. A fitting referral is specific, kind, and inside the director's role. It names the kind of help and how to reach it. A shove that says she needs therapy is the wrong tone.

distractorExplanations.a: Telling her she needs therapy as a shove, then cutting off the question, is the wrong tone. A referral is specific and kind, and it says how to reach the help.
distractorExplanations.b: Naming a suspected condition and supervising a treatment plan is diagnosis and treatment, outside the director's role. The referral points to help; it does not become the care.
distractorExplanations.c: A vague suggestion to look around town leaves her without a path. The referral names the kind of help and how to reach it, in language that is clear and kind.

prompt: A son lists anger, then bargaining, then sadness, and worries that his mother is behind because she has not reached acceptance ahead of Thursday's gathering. What should be said about those described stages?

options.text: Those stages are not a staircase anyone must climb in order
Tell him his mother must show acceptance before Thursday or the gathering has failed her
Score each relative on stages finished and delay the rite while anyone is still angry or sad
Drop the worry and use her unfinished place on the list as a reason to sell a larger gathering

explanation: The son is treating anger, bargaining, and sadness as a staircase his mother is late to finish before Thursday. Those stages are not a sequence the family must climb in order. She is not late, and acceptance is not a ticket the gathering requires.

distractorExplanations.b: Demanding acceptance before Thursday turns the stages into a deadline the family must hit. They are not an ordered staircase, and the gathering does not require her to arrive there.
distractorExplanations.c: Scoring relatives and delaying the rite enforces an order the stages do not have. Anger does not block the service, and the director does not grade the sequence.
distractorExplanations.d: Using her unfinished place to sell a larger gathering exploits the worry. The director does not sell from grief, and the stages are not a progress chart.

prompt: A niece asks to spend time with her uncle's body because part of her still expects him to walk through the door, and a coworker wants four mourning tasks scored before any such time is allowed. What is the useful point of her request?

options.text: Grade all four tasks in order and refuse the time with him until she passes each item on a checklist
Refuse the time with him, because wanting it shows she is dodging the reality of the death
Seeing him can serve the first task, accepting the loss is real
Assign the other tasks as graded homework due before burial and cancel the time beside him

explanation: She still expects him to walk in, and seeing him is one way some people take in that the death is real. That wish lines up with Worden's first task, accepting the reality of the loss. The four tasks are not a graded sequence the director enforces.

distractorExplanations.a: Grading all four tasks and blocking the visit turns the tasks into a test the director scores. The director does not enforce them as a sequence the family must pass.
distractorExplanations.b: Wanting to see him is often how someone begins to accept the death, not proof she is dodging it. Refusing the time fights the first task.
distractorExplanations.d: Homework and a canceled visit make the tasks a graded assignment due before burial. They describe mourning work; the director does not run them as a course.

prompt: At the doorway a cousin with a steady voice and dry eyes asks only what hour the visitation starts and which entrance the cars ought to use. She never mentions a feeling. Which kind of help matches that question?

options.text: Situational counseling that sets the hour and the door aside to sit with a feeling she never raised
A long life review that holds back the hour and the entrance until every memory in the lobby has been told
No answer at all, because giving a time and a door always counts as rushing a person's grief
Informational counseling: explain what happens next

explanation: She asked what hour visitation starts and which entrance to use, and she did not bring a feeling. That question needs informational counseling, which explains what will happen next. Situational counseling sits with a feeling, and she did not offer one.

distractorExplanations.a: Situational counseling sits with a feeling. She asked for a time and a door, which is a request for what happens next, so informational counseling is the match.
distractorExplanations.b: Holding back the hour for a life review ignores the question she asked. Informational counseling answers what happens next without turning a schedule question into a long session.
distractorExplanations.c: A factual answer to a factual question is not rushing. Refusing the time leaves her without the information she came to the door to get.

prompt: As scripture choices are discussed, a father says he believes his youngster is already at peace in a manner different from the arranger's private belief. His words are sincere and the plan breaks no rule. What belongs in this meeting?

options.text: Leave the family's belief uncorrected in this meeting
Stop the choices and debate doctrine until the father adopts the arranger's private belief about peace
Rewrite the readings so they teach the arranger's belief even though the father has objected
Reject any line that does not match the chapel's usual creed about what happens after death

explanation: The father has stated a sincere belief that his youngster is at peace, and the plan breaks no rule. The arrangement meeting is not the moment to correct a family's theology. The director carries the lawful wishes he has expressed.

distractorExplanations.b: Debating doctrine until he adopts the arranger's belief corrects his theology in the meeting. That correction is not the director's job while choices are being made.
distractorExplanations.c: Rewriting the readings to teach the arranger's belief overrides the father. The meeting carries his sincere, lawful wishes rather than a lesson in someone else's faith.
distractorExplanations.d: A house creed is not a test his lines must pass. Refusing his wording because it differs from chapel habit corrects his belief instead of arranging what he asked for.

prompt: A mother slams the folder, lifts her volume about a late start, and calls the delay a personal insult. The person across from her feels a pull to answer just as loudly. What is the better course?

options.text: Match her volume so she learns the firm will not be pushed around inside its own building by an angry client
End the meeting and tell her that anger means she is no longer a client who can decide anything here
Lower your voice and return to the decision; she is still the client
Win the argument about the late start before you touch any choice that is still sitting open on the table

explanation: She is angry about a late start, and the impulse is to answer at the same volume. An angry family is still the client. Matching that volume is the miss. Lower yours and return to the decision in front of you.

distractorExplanations.a: Matching her volume escalates the fight. Meeting anger with the same loudness is the miss. Lower the voice and go back to the decision she is still here to make.
distractorExplanations.b: Ending the meeting and dropping her treats anger as a reason to dismiss the client. She is still the client, and the work is the decision on the table.
distractorExplanations.d: Winning the clock argument puts your point ahead of her decision. Return to the choice in front of you instead of scoring the dispute about the late start.

prompt: After twenty minutes before a crowded display of burial containers, the grown children stare, switch topics, and still cannot settle on one. A brand-new coworker wants to wheel in three additional containers. What help is wiser?

options.text: Wheel in three more containers so a bigger display will force this stuck group to settle faster
Label the group difficult and let the person who complains least make the selection alone
Leave them with every container on the floor until embarrassment makes somebody point
Narrow the choice; overload is more likely than difficulty

explanation: They have stood in front of a full display and still cannot settle. A family that cannot choose is often overloaded, not difficult. Narrow the choice. Wheeling in three more containers makes the overload worse.

distractorExplanations.a: Adding three more containers widens a choice they already cannot make. Overload is the likelier cause, and the help is a smaller set, not a larger showroom.
distractorExplanations.b: Calling them difficult misreads paralysis as a character problem. They are overloaded, and handing the choice to the quietest person does not reduce that load.
distractorExplanations.c: Leaving them with every option until embarrassment forces a point uses shame. The director narrows the field so a decision is actually possible.

prompt: A dad asks if his eight-year-old may come see grandpa and what words should be used about the blossoms, the open box, and how motionless grandpa will appear. What guidance fits that dad's question?

options.text: Describe what the child will see, and let the parent decide
Ban every child from the building so none of them encounter the blossoms, the box, or grandpa
Say only that grandpa went on a trip, and give no concrete words about the room he would enter
Require the child to attend and to touch the box so the adults can see that coping has started

explanation: His dad is asking whether an eight-year-old may come and what to say about the blossoms, the box, and how still grandpa will look. Tell the child what he will see, in concrete words, and let the parent decide whether he attends. Do not ban every child.

distractorExplanations.b: Banning every child is a house rule the parent did not ask for. Attendance is the parent's decision, after the child hears concrete words about what the room contains.
distractorExplanations.c: A trip story hides the scene instead of describing it. Concrete words about what he will see prepare him, and the parent still decides whether he comes.
distractorExplanations.d: Requiring attendance and a touch takes the decision from the parent and turns the visit into a test. The parent decides, and nothing about coming is mandatory.

prompt: Two parents who just lost an infant at delivery sit holding a tiny blanket and admit they do not know how to tell neighbors. A bystander offers a bright remark about trying once more. What should be said instead?

options.text: Tell them they can have another baby, because a later birth will cancel the pain they feel in this room today
Treat the death as a minor file and move it faster than any other case that would cross the same desk
Honor this death as a real loss, and do not offer a replacement
Skip the infant and speak only about a later pregnancy they might try when they feel ready

explanation: They are holding a blanket after a baby died at birth and do not know how to tell people. A stillbirth or infant death is a real loss. The director does not answer with a line that they can have another.

distractorExplanations.a: Saying they can have another baby offers a replacement for the child who died. That sentence dismisses a real loss, and it is the line to avoid.
distractorExplanations.b: Speeding the file as if the death were minor treats an infant death as less than a loss. It is a real death and deserves the same care as any other.
distractorExplanations.d: Talking only about a later pregnancy erases the infant who died. The parents are mourning this baby, and the director does not point them at a replacement.

prompt: A spouse keeps repeating that an earlier call for the ambulance might have saved his wife, and he wants the arranger to declare the clinic at fault. Which reply stays inside the arranger's role?

options.text: Acknowledge the guilt without debating the care
Rebuild the ambulance timeline and rule on whether the clinic's care was right or wrong
Hand him steps that will erase the guilt before the morning of the rite arrives
Set the repetition aside as self-pity that does not belong beside the paperwork

explanation: He believes an earlier ambulance call might have saved his wife and wants the clinic declared at fault. Guilt of the 'if we had called sooner' kind gets acknowledgment. It does not get a debate about the medical care.

distractorExplanations.b: Ruling on the clinic's care debates the medical treatment. The director is not there to judge that care. The guilt gets acknowledgment, not a verdict.
distractorExplanations.c: Steps meant to erase the guilt before the rite treat the feeling as a task with a deadline. Acknowledgment stays with him; it does not schedule the guilt away.
distractorExplanations.d: Calling the words self-pity shuts the feeling down. The sentence is guilt, and the response is to acknowledge it, not to dismiss it as unworthy of the room.

prompt: On the day itself a sibling asks for a guarantee that by nightfall the whole group will feel done and ready to resume everyday habits. Which assurance is honest to give?

options.text: Promise that by nightfall the group will feel done and ready to resume everyday habits again
Guarantee the rite finishes mourning for every person who walks through the door today
Do not promise closure on the day of the funeral
Say the feeling of being done is delivered once the invoice has been paid in full

explanation: The sibling wants a guarantee that everyone will feel finished by nightfall. The director does not promise closure on the day of the funeral. The rite can help the family, and it does not end grief on a clock.

distractorExplanations.a: Promising they will feel done by nightfall is a closure promise tied to this day. Grief does not finish when the rite ends, and the director does not say it will.
distractorExplanations.b: Guaranteeing that the rite finishes mourning for everyone who attends is the same closure promise in a wider form. No service completes grief for every person present.
distractorExplanations.d: Tying a finished feeling to a paid invoice turns grief into a product. The director does not sell closure and does not promise it on the funeral day.

prompt: In the middle of a breakfast tale the cousins begin chuckling with clear fondness at his famously scorched pancakes, and the chuckling is aimed at him. An attendant steps forward to quiet the parlor. What response fits?

options.text: Let the fond humor stand unless it mocks someone else
Quiet them at once, because any laughter inside this parlor is disrespectful no matter how fond it sounds
Join by mocking the relative who sits silent and is not chuckling along with the cousins
Replace the breakfast tale with a stiff script that leaves no room for a smile in the parlor

explanation: The cousins are laughing with fondness at his scorched pancakes, and the laughter is about him. Humor from the family about the deceased can be love. Shutting it down as inappropriate is the miss, unless it mocks someone else in the room.

distractorExplanations.b: Hushing affectionate laughter treats love as disrespect. Humor about the deceased can be care. It is stopped when it mocks someone else, not when it remembers him warmly.
distractorExplanations.c: Mocking the silent relative aims the humor at another person in the room. Fond stories about the deceased can stand; mockery of someone present should not.
distractorExplanations.d: A script that bans every smile erases a loving memory. The miss is shutting down humor that is really affection for him.

prompt: Three siblings ask what emotion they are supposed to show today, since one feels nothing, one is furious, and one keeps making quips. They want a single proper feeling handed to them. What should they be given?

options.text: A numbered list of approved emotions they must display for guests before the doors open this afternoon
Orders for the numb sibling and the quipping sibling to copy the furious one so the group matches
Permission for whatever they feel, not a script
A warning that numbness and quips are failures they ought to hide from everyone who attends

explanation: One sibling feels nothing, one is furious, and one is joking, and they want the correct emotion assigned. A family that asks what they should feel gets permission for whatever they feel, not a script.

distractorExplanations.a: A list of approved emotions is a script. The director does not assign the right feeling. They get permission for numbness, anger, and jokes alike.
distractorExplanations.b: Ordering the others to copy the furious sibling forces one mood on the group. Permission means each feeling can stand, including numbness and quips.
distractorExplanations.d: Calling numbness and quips failures tells them their feelings are wrong. The answer is permission for whatever they feel, not a warning to hide it.

prompt: Riding away from the grave a staffer opens a prepaid-plan booklet for the worn-out partner and says the trip home should not be wasted. That stop was tagged as follow-up care. What has failed?

options.text: Aftercare used only to book a preneed fails its support purpose
Nothing failed, because worn-out sorrow on the ride from the grave is the best moment to close a prepaid plan
The ride home itself failed, because follow-up care must never include a practical trip
The timing failed, because the prepaid pitch should have landed in the middle of the spoken tribute

explanation: The staffer opened a prepaid booklet on the ride from the grave and called the trip follow-up care. Aftercare that exists only to book a preneed on the way home from the cemetery fails the support purpose it claims.

distractorExplanations.b: Calling fresh sorrow the best sales moment uses grief to book a preneed. Aftercare that exists only for that booking fails the support it was supposed to give.
distractorExplanations.c: A ride home can be real help. The failure is not the drive. The failure is turning the drive into a preneed sale and labeling that sale as care.
distractorExplanations.d: Moving the pitch into the tribute still uses the service to sell. Support fails whenever aftercare is only a preneed booking, whatever hour it happens.

prompt: A credentialed coworker reports that every initial notification now brings dread, a tight chest, and a hope the ringer will go unanswered. Both people are standing next to the preparation surface. What should the lead offer?

options.text: Put a clinical label on the dread beside the preparation surface, then send the same person back onto every first notification
Give a toughness talk that frames the dread as a personal flaw and send them straight back to the ringer
A schedule change or a colleague, not a diagnosis in this room
Start a private treatment hour led by the manager between cases, right there beside the preparation surface

explanation: Dread at every first notification, described beside the preparation surface, is a workload signal. That staff member needs a schedule change or a colleague. The lead does not deliver a diagnosis in the prep room.

distractorExplanations.a: Putting a clinical label on the dread beside the table is a diagnosis the lead should not make, and returning them to the same notifications ignores the schedule change they need.
distractorExplanations.b: A toughness talk treats dread as a character flaw. The useful offer is a different rota or a colleague beside them, not a lecture about weakness.
distractorExplanations.d: A treatment hour run by the manager in the prep room steps outside this role. The lead changes the schedule or pairs a colleague, and does not become the clinician.

prompt: A large kin group asks to keep vigil with a communal supper and stretches of loud singing in a parlor the premises can hold, and nothing they want violates any statute. A new hire starts refusing before any listening. What should happen instead?

options.text: Say the premises do not do that, without first hearing what the vigil, the supper, and the singing mean to them
Allow the loud singing even where a statute forbids it, because custom outranks every written rule on the books
Accommodate the vigil, supper, and singing when the building and the law allow it
Add an unlisted culture charge before anyone checks whether the parlor can actually hold the supper

explanation: They asked for a vigil with a shared supper and loud singing in a parlor the building can hold, and nothing they want breaks the law. Cultural mourning that includes a wake, a meal, or noise is accommodated when the building and the law allow it. Refusing without listening is the miss.

distractorExplanations.a: Saying the premises do not do that, before listening, is the miss. A wake, a meal, or noise is accommodated when the building and the law allow it.
distractorExplanations.b: Custom does not outrank statute. The firm accommodates the supper and the singing when the law allows them, and it does not carry a step the law forbids.
distractorExplanations.d: An unlisted culture charge is a surprise fee, not an answer to the request. Listen first, then host what the building and the law allow, with any real charge shown plainly.

prompt: The adult daughter sits down and asks which paper shows every charge before she chooses a single item. You hand her the home's General Price List at the start of the talk. What must that list name for her?

options.text: Only a package total, with the separate goods and services left unnamed
Casket styles alone, kept on a side sheet instead of the full list
Service titles, with every price withheld unless she specifically asks
The goods and services offered, each shown with its price

explanation: The General Price List names the goods and services the home offers and the price of each one. Giving her that list at the start is how she sees the charges before she chooses any item.

distractorExplanations.a: A package total that leaves the separate goods and services unnamed is not what the General Price List is required to show her.
distractorExplanations.b: Casket styles on a side sheet do not replace the General Price List, which has to name the goods and services and their prices.
distractorExplanations.c: Withholding prices until she asks hides the prices the list itself is supposed to name before she chooses.

prompt: A son wants the visitation but refuses the printed programs and the motorcycle escort inside a packaged offering. The arranger says the package cannot be taken apart and gives no disclosure of the pieces. What does itemizing allow this household to do?

options.text: Accept a sealed package that cannot be opened or disclosed
Buy the particular goods and services they actually want
Skip the required disclosures because a bundle feels simpler
Treat an unopened package as the only lawful way to buy

explanation: Itemizing lets this household buy the goods and services they want. A package they cannot take apart, offered without the required disclosures of its pieces, is the failure on this arrangement.

distractorExplanations.a: A sealed package that cannot be opened is the miss. Itemizing exists so the household can buy what they want, not a locked bundle.
distractorExplanations.c: Calling the bundle simpler does not erase the disclosures. Refusing to show the pieces is the mistake itemizing is meant to prevent.
distractorExplanations.d: Treating the unopened package as the only lawful purchase denies the choice itemizing is supposed to give this household.

prompt: After a busy month the bookkeeper still shows unpaid balances on completed calls and on preneed contracts whose billed amounts never arrived. The call count itself was high. What determines whether money is actually on hand?

options.text: A high call count, even while those balances stay uncollected
Collecting what is owed, including preneed and at-need
At-need balances only, with preneed amounts left uncounted
Finished calls alone, without regard to money still unpaid

explanation: Cash on hand depends on collecting what is owed, and that includes both preneed and at-need amounts. A high call count does not put money in the account while those balances remain unpaid.

distractorExplanations.a: A high call count records activity, not cash. Money is on hand only when the amounts owed, preneed and at-need, are actually collected.
distractorExplanations.c: Leaving preneed amounts out of the picture ignores half of what must be collected. Cash flow includes both preneed and at-need receivables.
distractorExplanations.d: Finished calls are not cash. Ignoring money still unpaid misses the collection of what is owed on preneed and at-need work.

prompt: An apprentice in the stock room asks which stored goods count as merchandise the firm sells, rather than hearses, the building, or money families still owe. Which goods belong in that merchandise inventory?

options.text: Hearses, the chapel building, and the preparation-room tables
Caskets, urns, and outer burial containers the home sells
Flower orders and obituary notices bought for one named family
Unpaid balances still sitting in accounts receivable

explanation: Merchandise inventory is the goods the home actually sells: caskets, urns, and outer burial containers. Vehicles, the building, cash-advance purchases, and unpaid balances are not that stock.

distractorExplanations.a: Hearses, the building, and preparation-room tables are fixed assets used to operate the firm, not merchandise inventory held for sale.
distractorExplanations.c: Flowers and obituary notices bought for one family are cash advances from outside vendors, not merchandise the home stocks and sells.
distractorExplanations.d: Unpaid balances are receivables, money owed to the firm, and they are a different asset from caskets, urns, and outer burial containers.

prompt: Friday afternoon the outer-container supplier reports it cannot make the Saturday committal the kin already chose. You can still reach the next of kin before that committal. What should you tell them?

options.text: Nothing yet, and quietly substitute a different container
That the Saturday committal must be canceled for good
That the vendor cannot deliver, and offer a real alternative
That the original container will appear if nobody asks

explanation: A vendor who cannot deliver for the Saturday committal is an operations problem. The next of kin should hear that fact and a real alternative, not a silent substitution or a canceled service.

distractorExplanations.a: A quiet substitution hides the vendor failure. The family has to hear that the supplier cannot deliver and be offered a real alternative.
distractorExplanations.b: Canceling the committal treats a delivery failure as the end of the service. The right step is to tell them and offer a real alternative.
distractorExplanations.d: Hoping the container appears if nobody asks is a silent substitution. They need the truth and a real alternative before Saturday.

prompt: Next week's roster covers the selection room in daytime hours and assigns nobody after dark. A nursing home will need an overnight transfer, and two rites plus planning meetings are already booked. What must that roster include?

options.text: Daytime showroom coverage, with night transfers left until morning
Planning meetings and rites only, with transfers and preparation left out
Visitations in the afternoon, and no one on call after dark
The first call, the arrangement, the preparation, and the service

explanation: The roster has to cover the first call, the arrangement, the preparation, and the service. A selection room staffed only in daytime, with nobody on call after dark, fails the overnight transfer.

distractorExplanations.a: Leaving night transfers until morning fails the first call. The roster must cover that call along with the arrangement, the preparation, and the service.
distractorExplanations.b: Planning meetings and rites are only part of the work. Dropping transfers and preparation leaves the first call and the preparation uncovered.
distractorExplanations.c: Afternoon visitations with no one on call after dark repeat the failure. An overnight transfer needs a roster that includes the first call.

prompt: A brother stands in the lobby, upset that the procession left the church later than he was promised, and other guests can hear every word. He wants an answer today. How should his complaint be handled?

options.text: Argue the timeline with him in the lobby while guests listen
Keep the exchange verbal so the file shows no complaint
Write it down, answer promptly, and follow the home's policy
Wait several days so the anger fades before anyone responds

explanation: His complaint should be written down, answered promptly, and handled under the home's policy. Arguing the timeline in the lobby, where other guests can hear, is the miss.

distractorExplanations.a: Arguing the timeline in the lobby, in front of other guests, escalates the complaint instead of writing it down and following the home's policy.
distractorExplanations.b: Keeping the exchange verbal leaves no record. A complaint is written down, answered promptly, and handled under the home's policy.
distractorExplanations.d: Waiting several days for the anger to fade is a delay. The complaint needs a prompt answer under the home's policy, not a postponed reply.

prompt: A draft radio spot says the statute requires every buyer to purchase a sealing casket, and the same sentence appears in the script arrangers are told to read aloud. What must that advertising and that script avoid?

options.text: Claiming the law requires a product it does not require
Mentioning a price that the General Price List already prints
Hosting an evening seminar about planning ahead
Citing a competitor's published price when that price is accurate

explanation: The radio spot and the arrangement script must not claim the law requires a sealing casket, or any product the law does not require. That false legal claim is the advertising mistake.

distractorExplanations.b: Mentioning a price the General Price List already prints is not the problem. The miss is claiming the law requires a product it does not require.
distractorExplanations.c: An evening planning seminar is ordinary outreach. It is not the deceptive legal claim this radio spot and script have to avoid.
distractorExplanations.d: An accurate citation of a competitor's published price is not a false legal requirement. The script must not invent a duty the statute does not impose.

prompt: The widow believes the grave opening, the marker setting, and your service fee are one invoice from one licensed company. The cemetery is a different company. How are these two businesses usually related?

options.text: As one firm, because a funeral license automatically covers the cemetery
As identical shops, because the cemetery also directs the funeral
Often as separate businesses, with separate charges and licenses where the state requires them
As one price sheet, because cemetery fees must be restated as funeral-home prices

explanation: A cemetery and a funeral home are often separate businesses, with separate charges and, where the state requires it, separate licenses. Her grave opening and marker setting are not automatically your invoice.

distractorExplanations.a: A funeral license does not automatically cover the cemetery. The two are often separate businesses with separate charges and, where the state says so, separate licenses.
distractorExplanations.b: The cemetery is not an identical shop that directs the funeral. Interment charges and funeral charges commonly come from different firms.
distractorExplanations.d: Restating cemetery fees as funeral-home prices collapses two bills into one. The charges stay separate when the businesses are separate.

prompt: After a difficult house call, a new licensee wants praise for speed and plans to add the missing identification band and unsigned permission later. What does risk control still require on this file?

options.text: Speed alone, if the household later says it is grateful
A spoken okay in place of the signed authorization
An insurance policy instead of a file or prep-room safety steps
Identification, signed authorizations, prep-room OSHA practice, and a file

explanation: Risk control on this file is identification, signed authorizations, OSHA practice in the preparation room, and a written file. Speed without the band and the signed permission is the miss.

distractorExplanations.a: Gratitude for speed does not replace the identification band. Risk control still requires identification, signed authorizations, prep-room OSHA practice, and a file.
distractorExplanations.b: A spoken okay leaves no signed authorization. Heroics without that form fail the file that risk control requires.
distractorExplanations.c: An insurance policy does not stand in for the file or for OSHA practice in the preparation room. Those controls still have to be done.

prompt: Coworkers have been posting updates in a phone thread about the burial permit, whether the bill was paid, and which forms remain open. None of that is in the record. What should the case-management system track?

options.text: The file, the forms, the money, and the compliance tasks
Social posts about the rite, and not the case record
The money only, kept apart from forms and compliance tasks
The phone thread, treated as the official case file

explanation: The case-management system tracks the file, the forms, the money, and the compliance tasks. A phone thread about the permit and the bill is not the file, even if the updates feel current.

distractorExplanations.b: Social posts about the rite are not the case record. The system has to track the file, the forms, the money, and the compliance tasks.
distractorExplanations.c: Keeping the money apart from the forms and the compliance tasks splits the file. The system is supposed to track all of those together.
distractorExplanations.d: Treating the phone thread as the official file leaves the record empty. Compliance tasks, forms, and money belong in the case-management system.

prompt: A licensee whose credential expires next quarter insists continuing education is optional after the national board examination and that renewal never depends on it. How do state rules actually treat that education?

options.text: Federal trade rules impose it on every director in every state
Passing the national board examination ends any renewal duty
Many states require it to renew a funeral director license
It can replace the national board examination for a first license

explanation: Many states require continuing education before a funeral director license can be renewed. Passing the national board examination does not make renewal education optional in those states, and not every state uses the same rule.

distractorExplanations.a: Continuing education for license renewal is a state rule, not a federal trade rule imposed on every director in every state.
distractorExplanations.b: Passing the national board examination does not end the renewal duty in states that require continuing education to keep the funeral director license.
distractorExplanations.d: Continuing education maintains a license that already exists. It does not replace the national board examination for someone seeking a first license.

prompt: These relatives described a simple visitation and stated the spending limit they can live with. You are about to suggest a casket from the display. Which suggestion is ethical?

options.text: Lead with the highest-priced casket after they named a limit
Tell them the law requires a casket for the rite they described
Hide the prices until they have already pointed at a casket
Follow what they said they need, and do not coerce them

explanation: The ethical suggestion follows what these relatives said they need, including the spending limit they named. Pushing the highest-priced casket after they set that limit is coercion.

distractorExplanations.a: Leading with the highest-priced casket after they named a spending limit is coercion. The suggestion has to follow what they said they need.
distractorExplanations.b: Telling them the law requires a casket for the rite they described invents a legal duty. The recommendation still has to follow their stated needs.
distractorExplanations.c: Hiding prices until they point at a casket withholds the information they need. An ethical suggestion follows what they said they need, without that pressure.

prompt: The county hospital phones at midnight and asks you to take their patient to your building. The next of kin is still driving in with papers, and the desk has not released the patient. What must occur before you leave with the deceased?

options.text: A fast departure now, with identification postponed until morning
Leaving at once, because the hospital call itself is the authorization
Departure while the release and the notifications are still unfinished
A respectful removal plus the notifications and authorizations required

explanation: The first call is a respectful removal plus the notifications and authorizations that have to happen before you leave with the deceased. The hospital phone call does not replace the release or those authorizations.

distractorExplanations.a: Postponing identification until morning skips part of the removal. The required notifications and authorizations have to be done before you leave with the deceased.
distractorExplanations.b: The hospital call is a request, not the authorization. You still need the notifications and authorizations before a respectful removal leaves with the deceased.
distractorExplanations.c: Leaving while the release and the notifications are unfinished skips the steps that must be done before you take the deceased.

prompt: Three siblings cannot agree on visitation hours, music, or whether anyone will speak. The price sheets are on the table and the calendar holds one hour. What does a sound planning meeting do?

options.text: Explain the options, listen, and write down what they chose
Present one complete package and move straight to a signature
Keep the price sheets back until every choice is already locked
Collect signatures before anyone has explained the costs

explanation: A sound planning meeting explains the options, listens to the siblings while they disagree, and writes down what they chose. Rushing a signature before that conversation is the miss.

distractorExplanations.b: Presenting one complete package and moving straight to a signature skips the listening. The meeting should explain the options and record what they chose.
distractorExplanations.c: Keeping the price sheets back until choices are locked reverses the meeting. Options and prices come first, then you write down what they chose.
distractorExplanations.d: Collecting signatures before the costs are explained leaves the choices undocumented in any real sense. Explain, listen, then write down what they chose.

prompt: A caller asks whether cremation with no gathering is available. The sheet you mailed hides that choice in tiny type on the final page, while a full traditional rite fills the opening page. Where must both choices appear?

options.text: Only the traditional rite on the front, with direct cremation omitted from the list entirely
By telephone only, so direct cremation never has to be printed for people who do not ask
In tiny type on the final page, so the traditional rite is what callers notice first
Both on the General Price List, where they can be seen

explanation: Direct cremation and a full traditional rite both belong on the General Price List, where a caller can see them. Hiding direct cremation in tiny type on the final page is the miss.

distractorExplanations.a: Omitting direct cremation from the list entirely hides an offering that belongs on the General Price List beside the traditional rite.
distractorExplanations.b: Keeping direct cremation as a telephone-only remark leaves it off the printed list. Both offerings have to appear where the caller can see them.
distractorExplanations.c: Tiny type on the final page is the hiding place this sheet already uses. Both choices belong on the General Price List in a form people can actually see.

prompt: The cousins want to walk among the caskets immediately. Nobody has shown them the casket price sheet, and a colleague is holding the selection-room door. At what point may they go in?

options.text: Only after they have seen the casket prices
Immediately, before any casket price sheet is shown, so they choose by appearance alone
After they point to a casket, so the price sheet cannot influence the choice
Whenever the door is open, because the price sheet is optional once they are in the room

explanation: They may enter the casket selection room only after they have seen the casket prices. Opening the door first, and showing prices later or not at all, reverses the order the Rule requires.

distractorExplanations.b: Walking in before any casket price sheet is shown reverses the required order. Prices come first, and only then may they enter the selection room.
distractorExplanations.c: Letting them point to a casket before they see prices makes the price sheet an afterthought. The Rule's order is prices first, then the room.
distractorExplanations.d: An open door does not make the price sheet optional. They enter only after the casket prices have been shown.

prompt: You quote one package for a chapel rite. When the daughter asks which pieces sit inside that package, you answer that a bundle is simply easier. She still cannot see the contents. What must you still provide?

options.text: Nothing further, because saying a bundle is easier replaces the need to name the contents
A clear list of what the package price includes
Removal of the package from the price list once she seems comfortable
The word bundle by itself, treated as a full description of the goods and services inside

explanation: A package price still has to show what is included. Telling her a bundle is simply easier, without a list of the pieces, leaves her unable to see the contents she asked about.

distractorExplanations.a: Saying a bundle is easier does not replace the list. She still has to see what the package price includes.
distractorExplanations.c: Removing the package from the price list does not answer which pieces are inside it. The contents still have to be shown.
distractorExplanations.d: The word bundle is not a description of the goods and services inside. A package price still has to let her see what is included.

prompt: The newspaper's invoice for the death notice is in the folder. Your draft statement lists a cash-advance line for that notice, the two amounts differ, and nobody explained an added charge. How should the cash advance be shown?

options.text: At a higher amount, with the difference kept and never explained to anyone
Left off the statement, because the newspaper billed the funeral home rather than the household
At the newspaper's charge, plus only a markup you disclose
At a round figure that need not match the invoice, since cash advances are estimates

explanation: The obituary cash advance is listed at the amount the newspaper charges, plus any markup you disclose. Keeping an undisclosed difference between the invoice and the statement is the miss.

distractorExplanations.a: A higher amount with the difference kept and never explained is an undisclosed markup. The line should be the newspaper's charge plus only a markup you disclose.
distractorExplanations.b: Leaving the notice off the statement hides a cash advance the household is paying through you. It still belongs on the statement at the newspaper's charge.
distractorExplanations.d: A round figure that ignores the invoice pockets a difference nobody explained. The cash advance follows the newspaper's charge, plus only a disclosed markup.

prompt: They ask you to book their pastor, a soloist, and the florist they already named. Each of those people will bill for work these relatives chose. How do those outside charges belong on the contract?

options.text: As your own service fees, with the outside bills absorbed and never shown
As rough estimates that need not be labeled cash advances or tied to their vendors
As showroom merchandise, because you were the person who placed the calls
As their own vendors or as disclosed cash advances

explanation: Clergy, the soloist, and flowers the relatives order through you are either their own vendors or disclosed cash advances. Absorbing those bills into your service fees hides whose charge it is.

distractorExplanations.a: Absorbing the pastor, soloist, and florist into your own service fees hides charges that are either their vendors or disclosed cash advances.
distractorExplanations.b: Rough estimates that are not labeled leave the cash-advance disclosure undone. Those outside charges are their vendors or disclosed cash advances.
distractorExplanations.c: Placing the calls does not turn clergy, music, and flowers into showroom merchandise. They remain the family's vendors or disclosed cash advances.

prompt: At eleven at night a daughter requests a transfer from the residence before morning. Nobody is on the transfer rotation and the van is unmanned. Promising a sunrise arrival ignores what she asked. What does answering this request require?

options.text: A staffed removal vehicle, or an honest alternative
A promise to arrive in the morning, with no alternative offered for the night removal she requested
An ended call that tells her nothing about what can actually be done before morning
A request that she keep the deceased at home until some vehicle happens to be free

explanation: Being able to serve this night request means a removal vehicle and a staffed first-call rotation, or an honest alternative when those are not available. A sunrise promise that ignores her request is the miss.

distractorExplanations.b: Promising a morning arrival with no alternative ignores the night removal she asked for. She needs a staffed vehicle or an honest alternative tonight.
distractorExplanations.c: Ending the call without saying what can be done leaves her with no alternative. The response has to be a staffed removal or an honest option she can use.
distractorExplanations.d: Asking her to keep the deceased at home until a vehicle is free is not an honest alternative. Serving the call means a staffed removal vehicle or a real option tonight.

prompt: The lines on the father's statement use the amounts printed for each selected item, yet the handwritten sum at the foot of the page is not those lines added together. He is ready to sign. What happens before that signature?

options.text: He signs now, and the sum is quietly changed after he leaves the room
The sum is corrected so it matches the list prices
The printed line prices are scratched out so they equal the handwritten sum
He signs the mismatched sum, with a note that the arithmetic can be repaired later

explanation: The statement he signs has to match the prices on the General Price List. A handwritten sum that is not the total of those lines is corrected before he signs, not afterward.

distractorExplanations.a: Changing the sum after he leaves means he signed a total that did not add up. The correction has to happen before the signature.
distractorExplanations.c: Scratching out the printed line prices to match a bad sum abandons the General Price List. The sum is what gets corrected so it matches those prices.
distractorExplanations.d: A note that arithmetic can be repaired later still lets him sign a total that does not add up. Fix the sum before the signature.

prompt: A prearrangement check arrives during a week when payroll is tight. Someone proposes dropping it into the operating account and restoring it after the next collection. Which rules control that check?

options.text: The operating account, whenever payroll is short, as long as you intend to replace the money later
The manager's preference, because prearrangement money is ordinary revenue in the week it arrives
That state's trusting or insurance rules
A drawer in the arrangement office until someone chooses a convenient account

explanation: Preneed funds are handled under that state's trusting or insurance rules. A tight payroll week is not a reason to drop the check into the operating account and plan to restore it later.

distractorExplanations.a: Intending to replace the money later does not make the operating account lawful. The check follows that state's trusting or insurance rules, not this week's payroll gap.
distractorExplanations.b: Prearrangement money is not ordinary revenue the manager may prefer to spend. State trusting or insurance rules control where that check goes.
distractorExplanations.d: A drawer in the arrangement office is not a trusting arrangement. The check is handled under that state's trusting or insurance rules.

prompt: Someone comparing two firms by telephone asks what you charge for cremation without a rite and for a full traditional rite. You are not standing in the selection room. Which figures do you quote?

options.text: Lower telephone estimates that you can raise once they walk into the building
A vague range only, because exact figures are reserved for people who visit in person
The other firm's figures, so the comparison never has to use your own list
The same prices you would quote inside the building

explanation: A household comparing two firms on the telephone gets the same prices you would quote inside the building. Lower estimates, a vague range, or the other firm's figures are not that quote.

distractorExplanations.a: Lower telephone estimates that rise once they walk in are a different price from the one you would quote in the building. The figures have to match.
distractorExplanations.b: A vague range reserved for visitors withholds the prices. The telephone quote is the same prices you would give inside the building.
distractorExplanations.c: Quoting the other firm's figures dodges your own list. The caller should hear the same prices you would quote in your building.

prompt: Before a newly hired arranger meets relatives, the owner says to leave every charge unexplained and to step out and ask the owner before naming any amount. What must people who sit with relatives be able to do?

options.text: Explain the General Price List themselves
Sit through the meeting unable to state a price until the owner is reached on every line
Read names on the list while refusing to explain what any charge includes
Postpone the entire meeting until the owner can recite each price in person

explanation: Staff who meet relatives need to be able to explain the General Price List. Sending the new arranger in with instructions to check with the owner on every price stalls the purpose of having the list in the room.

distractorExplanations.b: Leaving the arranger unable to state a price until the owner is reached on every line stalls the meeting. Staff who sit with relatives should explain the list themselves.
distractorExplanations.c: Reading names while refusing to explain the charges is not an explanation of the General Price List. The people in the room have to be able to explain it.
distractorExplanations.d: Postponing the meeting so the owner can recite each price admits the arranger cannot explain the list. That explanation is part of the arranger's job.

prompt: Yesterday's setup casket is still sitting in the chapel. Today's relatives chose a different casket and never mentioned the one already in the room. A colleague wants it added to their paperwork anyway. Which merchandise may the contract list?

options.text: Any casket already placed in the chapel, even though these relatives never selected it
Only merchandise this family actually selected
Both caskets, so the paperwork mirrors everything physically present in the building
The leftover chapel casket, because setup goods transfer automatically to the next household

explanation: The contract lists merchandise this family actually selected. The casket already sitting in the chapel was not their choice, so it does not appear on their paperwork because it happened to be in the room.

distractorExplanations.a: A casket already placed in the chapel is not theirs if they never selected it. The contract lists only the merchandise this family actually chose.
distractorExplanations.c: Listing both caskets because both are in the building charges them for goods they did not select. Only their selection belongs on the contract.
distractorExplanations.d: Setup goods do not transfer automatically to the next household. Merchandise they did not select stays off their contract.

prompt: These relatives reach the office long after the scheduled start, following a hard morning at the clinic. A coworker wants to add a charge titled grief delay fee. Those words appear nowhere on the printed price sheet. Can you add that charge?

options.text: Yes, if the lateness inconvenienced the staff, even though that fee is not listed anywhere
Yes, by renaming the wait as a cash advance and writing it onto the statement at the table
Yes, if you announce the fee out loud before they sit, even though the price sheet omits it
No, because that fee is not on the General Price List

explanation: A late arrival is not a reason to bill a grief delay fee that is not on the General Price List. Inconvenience, a new name, or a spoken announcement does not create a charge the list does not contain.

distractorExplanations.a: Staff inconvenience does not create a charge. A grief delay fee that is not on the General Price List cannot be added because they arrived late.
distractorExplanations.b: Renaming the wait as a cash advance still invents a fee that is not on the General Price List. A late family is not billed that made-up charge.
distractorExplanations.c: Announcing the fee out loud does not put it on the General Price List. If the price sheet omits it, you do not add it at the table.

prompt: From the spouse at the residence you accept a suit, a wedding band, and a wristwatch. Several days later the spouse asks which of those items were given back, and the removal notes are silent. What should have been written down?

options.text: The clothing, jewelry, and personal effects received and returned
Only the time of arrival, leaving the suit, band, and watch to memory
A guess at what the jewelry might sell for, instead of what was received and what was returned
A spoken promise to the spouse, with no written list of items taken or handed back

explanation: The director documents the clothing, jewelry, and personal effects received at the removal, and what was returned. Silent notes leave the spouse unable to learn which of the suit, band, and watch came back.

distractorExplanations.b: Recording only the time of arrival leaves the suit, band, and watch to memory. Clothing, jewelry, and personal effects received and returned belong in the notes.
distractorExplanations.c: Guessing what the jewelry might sell for is not the record. The notes should say what was received and what was returned, not a resale guess.
distractorExplanations.d: A spoken promise with no written list is how these notes went silent. The director writes down the effects received and the effects returned.

prompt: A civic club wants a short notice in the community column before anyone has said which facts may be released to the public. The planning visit is tomorrow. When is that notice allowed to be sent?

options.text: Immediately, because a community column is different from an obituary the household buys
As soon as the club asks, using every fact the hospital included on the first call
Tonight, including age and address, so the household can edit the notice after it has already run
Only after the family says what may be public

explanation: A community death notice is not sent until the family has said what may be public. The club's request, the hospital's first-call facts, and a plan to edit later do not authorize the notice tomorrow's visit has not yet approved.

distractorExplanations.a: Calling it a community column instead of a paid obituary does not make it public. The notice waits until the family says what may be released.
distractorExplanations.b: The hospital's first-call facts are not the family's permission. Sending the notice as soon as the club asks releases details nobody has approved.
distractorExplanations.c: Running age and address tonight, and letting them edit afterward, publishes facts before the family has said what may be public.

prompt: The brother signs a statement that is still blank, and by the next afternoon he cannot name the selections, the cost, or the sequence of events. What would a sound meeting have left him able to describe?

options.text: Only that he signed quickly, with the selections filled in by staff after he left
The blank page itself, which staff will complete once he is out of the building
A promise that someone will telephone later with the prices and the schedule
What he bought, what it costs, and what happens next

explanation: A quality meeting leaves him able to describe, the next day, what he bought, what it costs, and what happens next. A fast signature on a blank statement is the failure, because he cannot describe any of those three.

distractorExplanations.a: A quick signature with selections filled in after he left is the blank-statement failure. He should leave able to describe what he bought, the cost, and what happens next.
distractorExplanations.b: Completing a blank page after he is out of the building means he signed without knowing the selections. The meeting should leave those facts with him.
distractorExplanations.c: A later telephone call is not a substitute for the meeting. He should already be able to describe what he bought, what it costs, and what happens next.
